objective: The acceptance suite of conversations (package 20.10): written people, one or more per family, each played from the first sentence to the holdout number the way the product runs (a draft per file, the coordinator walking it with the person answering, the build, the Solution page saved with what the person states, every stage run by the engine; no model). Scored on the problem card, the workflow (it validates and the graph refused no move), the pipeline (every step run, none stale) and the holdout (the kind's acceptance decisions against the replica's planted truth); a family the engine does not run is right when its build is refused with the reason. Dev: 15 people, written beside the rules. Sealed: 30 people, written by a separate agent from a brief of the replicas (their columns, moments and the Solution form's statements) without reading the rules, the dev people or any code; their SHA-256 was pinned before any run. The kind's own fields (a forecast's horizon, an entity table's cutoffs) are stated by the person on the Solution page, not read from the conversation. Results: dev JRN-001, 15 of 15 (written beside the rules: not evidence). Sealed JRN-002 (gate journeys_gate_v1, replica seed 1, run once): 16 of 30 right, 95% interval 0.361 to 0.698, no move refused: fail. Right on all 12 classification, regression and segmentation journeys; 14 misses: 11 on the card (people's own words for anomaly, time to event, uplift, ranking, streams, entity tables and text that the rules do not read: "spotting fake rides", "how long will a subscriber stick around", "the difference the offer makes"), 2 on the holdout (a rare event's review budget never asked within five questions; a forecast whose moment, paraphrased, no longer said the weather is measured on the day), and their builds. The set is spent; nothing is tuned on it.
rule: Scores say how DCLab carries these written people over these seeded replicas, not how it handles any other person or table, and nothing about production readiness. The dev score is not evidence: it was written beside the rules. The sealed writer is a model instance, not a person: an independent human writer remains the owner's decision.
